name: Pet shops and pet supplies

problems.words: Regular customers' food brand runs out and they switch to another shop
quick_ideas: List the brands your regulars buy most, because those are the ones you can't run out of
Compare distributor lead time with how fast they sell, because it sets your real reorder point.

workzap_build.text: food stock by brand and size with reorder alerts based on sales speed and lead time.

problems.ask_first: Is it mostly imported brands that run out?
problems.free_stops: reorder levels per brand are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every time a regular asks for a missing food brand this week, so you see which empty shelf sends loyal buyers elsewhere.
Give one person a single reorder page for regulars' food brands, so the fastest moving favourites are checked before they run out.

problems.words: Customers order every month but we don't remind them, so they go elsewhere
quick_ideas: Ask regulars if they'd like a reminder when they're due, saving numbers only with their permission
Note each regular's usual cycle, because timing matters more than frequency.

workzap_build.text: repeat-order reminders timed to each opted-in customer's cycle, with one-tap reorder.

problems.free_stops: reminder timing and reorder flow are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare this week's repeat orders with last month's usual busy days, so you spot where missed reminders are losing routine monthly sales.
Give one person a fixed time each day to check the repeat order notebook, so monthly buyers are not missed when the shop gets busy.

problems.words: Bags of food expire in the storeroom
quick_ideas: Do one expiry sweep and move the earliest stock forward, because new stock often sells first
List what expires soon, so it can be moved in time.

workzap_build.text: expiry tracking with first-expiry-first-out alerts across branches.

problems.free_stops: alert timing is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many food bags in the storeroom expire before the front shelf stock, so you see whether older stock is being stranded behind.
Give one staff member the weekly storeroom expiry walk and one notebook page, so soon expiring bags get moved before they become waste.

problems.words: Grooming bookings clash and groomers are double-booked
quick_ideas: Move all bookings into one shared diary, because clashes come from separate books
Note how long each service really takes, because slots are often set too short.

workzap_build.text: a grooming and boarding calendar with groomer schedules and reminders.

problems.free_stops: slot design and reminder flow go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each time two grooming bookings overlap this week, so you can see which services or staff create the clashes.
Give one person the job of writing every grooming booking in one diary, so double booking stops when messages come from different places.

problems.words: Tank cleaning and feeding schedules get skipped when staff are off
quick_ideas: Write down every daily care task and who owns it, because gaps appear when nobody is named
Have staff sign off once a day, because it shows what was missed.

workzap_build.text: a daily care checklist on phone with staff sign-off and an alert to the owner when tasks are missed.

problems.ask_first: Who looks after the animals each day?
problems.free_stops: the checklist and alert setup are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count which tank cleaning and feeding tasks were skipped on staff off days this week, so the weakest cover points become visible.
Give one person each shift the care notebook handover, so tank cleaning and feeding still happen when the usual staff are away.

problems.words: Delivery orders for heavy litter bags cost more than they earn
quick_ideas: Work out what one delivery actually costs you, because it shows which orders lose money
Group deliveries by area, because fewer trips cost less.

workzap_build.text: a delivery planner grouping orders by area with rider assignment and cost per delivery.

problems.ask_first: Who delivers, your riders or a courier?
problems.free_stops: routing and delivery pricing rules go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which heavy litter deliveries needed separate trips this week, so you can see which orders eat time and fuel.
Give one person the daily delivery list in one notebook, so nearby heavy orders leave together instead of as costly extra runs.

problems.words: Fish and birds die in the shop and we don't track the loss
quick_ideas: Record every loss for a month, because it shows the real cost
Note conditions alongside, because patterns help you and your vet see what's going on.

workzap_build.text: a live-stock loss log with monthly cost.

problems.ask_first: Do you sell live animals regularly?
problems.free_stops: the log and reporting design are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Tally missing saleable stock in each cage and tank area at closing this week, so the worst loss point for margin shows.
Give one staff member the closing stock loss note in one notebook every evening, so loss recording stays consistent across shifts.

problems.words: Delivery app listings show wrong stock
quick_ideas: Compare the shelf count with the listed count for your fastest selling pet items once, so you see how often shoppers meet wrong stock.
Give one person a fixed time to check listed stock against the shelf notebook, so online availability stays closer to what you can actually sell.

workzap_build.text: stock synced to Talabat, Noon or Instashop listings so items you don't have aren't shown.

problems.ask_first: Which apps do you sell on?
problems.free_stops: connections per app are detailed in the solution document.
quick_ideas_original: Check your top items on each app once, because it shows how far they've drifted
Make one person own app stock, because otherwise nobody updates.

problems.words: Imported food stuck at customs, shelves empty for weeks
quick_ideas: List expected shipments with dates, because it shows where gaps are coming
Keep a local alternative in mind for key lines, because regulars need something on the shelf.

workzap_build.text: a supplier tracker for imported shipments with expected dates and alerts.

problems.ask_first: Do you import directly or through distributors?
problems.free_stops: tracking setup is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which imported food lines customers asked for during empty shelf days, so you see which gaps are hurting regular demand most.
Give one person one page for expected imported food arrivals and shelf gaps, so staff stop guessing what is delayed and what is sold out.

problems.words: Customer data is only on staff phones
quick_ideas: Move regulars into a shop record, with their permission, because the relationship then stays with the shop
Agree a rule that shop orders use the shop number, because personal phones leave with staff.

workzap_build.text: a shop-owned consented customer list with visits and purchases.

problems.ask_first: How many staff take orders on their own phones?
problems.free_stops: setup and consent flow go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many repeat orders this week arrived through personal staff numbers, so you see how much customer follow up sits off shop records.
Give one staff member a notebook beside the till for repeat order details, so the shop keeps the buying pattern when staff change.

never_say: Any veterinary, diet, dosing, medication or breeding advice; for an animal in distress, say contact a vet urgently.
Advice on animal import or export permits, licensing or welfare law.
Help with trade in protected, wild or illegally imported animals.
Anything requiring customers' names, addresses or pet records in the chat.
For serious bites, fire or chemical exposure, anything other than "call emergency services".

sample_reply.person: My regulars buy the same premium food every month, but when it's out they just go elsewhere. What can I do?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this can be fixed. 1. List the brands your regulars buy most, because those are the ones you can't run out of. 2. Compare your distributor's delivery time with how fast each sells, which shows when you really need to reorder. Workzap can do this automatically for you: stock alerts based on real sales speed, and reminders to regulars who opt in when their food is due. Would you like me to arrange a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
